summary: Cypriot authorities closed the Ledra Street–Lokmaci pedestrian crossing in Nicosia on 29 February 2020 as a precaution against COVID-19. summary: Switzerland extended its COVID-19 entry restrictions to its borders with Germany, Austria and France on 17 March 2020. summary: Denmark began refusing entry to foreign travellers without an accepted essential purpose on 14 March 2020 to limit COVID-19 transmission. summary: Poland restricted foreign passenger entry from 15 March 2020 to reduce the spread of COVID-19 and suspended international passenger rail services. summary: Serbia tightened its COVID-19 border restrictions on 20 March 2020, closing passenger entry to citizens as well as foreigners while continuing to admit trucks and specially authorised travellers. summary: Montenegro prohibited entry by most foreign passengers on 15 March 2020 to prevent COVID-19 transmission. summary: Spanish authorities restricted nonessential movement at the La Línea–Gibraltar frontier during the March 2020 COVID-19 emergency. summary: The Czech government barred ordinary departures by citizens and residents from 16 March 2020 as part of its COVID-19 measures, alongside restrictions on foreign entry. summary: North Macedonia restricted entry by foreign passengers at its land crossings in mid-March 2020 to prevent COVID-19 transmission. summary: Norway restricted entry by foreign nationals from 16 March 2020 to limit COVID-19 transmission, while exempting citizens, qualifying residents and specified work, family and transport groups. summary: Portugal and Spain restricted nonessential cross-border movement from the night of 16–17 March 2020 to contain COVID-19. summary: Germany began rejecting travellers without an urgent reason at its Austrian, Swiss, French, Luxembourg and Danish borders on 16 March 2020 to curb COVID-19. summary: The Republic of Cyprus suspended passage at Deryneia, Astromeritis–Zodhia and Lefka–Apliki on 29 February 2020 as a COVID-19 precaution. verification.notes: Checked widened categories, exemptions and September limited relaxation with designated-post restriction.

summary: France required compelling reasons for travel to and from the United Kingdom from 18 December 2021 in response to the Omicron variant. The restriction applied even to vaccinated tourists and business travellers, with exceptions including French nationals and immediate family returning home. Vaccinated arrivals into France no longer needed a compelling reason from 14 January 2022. Unvaccinated travellers still faced different rules, and the Channel Tunnel itself was not completely closed.

verification.notes: Checked bidirectional initial rule versus vaccinated inbound endpoint and avoided throughput-closure claim.

summary: Polish truckers restricted commercial freight at the Korczowa, Hrebenne and Dorohusk approaches to Ukraine from November 2023, protesting transport-market competition and permit and queue rules. Some trucks continued under quotas, while humanitarian, military and other specified loads were exempt; passengers were not generally barred. Dorohusk reopened briefly in December before the blockade resumed. The three approaches returned to normal processing on 16 January 2024, following their different interruption histories.

verification.notes: Checked three-post campaign, Dorohusk December gap, selective throughput and actual January endpoint.

summary: Polish farmers restricted truck traffic at four Lubelskie approaches to Ukraine from February 2024, protesting EU environmental policies and Ukrainian agricultural imports. Quotas, weight limits and directions varied by crossing, while cars, buses and specified essential consignments generally continued. The protests ended at different times during March and April, with an interruption and restart at Dołhobyczów and the last Hrebenne restrictions ending around 28–29 April. Separate grain-import rules remained afterward.

verification.notes: Checked five restriction periods, changing throughput and separate underlying import ban; retained Hrebenne endpoint bound.

summary: Russia ordered the suspension of people, vehicles, goods and cargo through seven named railway border posts from 1 July 2026. Five faced Finland, with Pechory-Pskovskie facing Estonia and Pytalovo facing Latvia; other railway routes were outside the order. The government instrument did not state a reason. Later legal information retained the suspension, but the evidence does not establish that every listed facility had been operating immediately before the order.

verification.notes: Checked July operative date, seven-post list, continuing qualified legal status and absence of stated motive.

summary: Bosnia and Herzegovina introduced COVID-19 entry restrictions for specified origins in March 2020, then broadened them to most nonexempt foreign visitors later that month. Citizens and authorised residence, work, medical, freight and transit categories retained access. Croatian, Serbian and Montenegrin nationals were permitted again from 28 May, with broader conditional admission following in September. The changes concerned entry eligibility and did not close every border post to all movement.

verification.notes: Checked staged March scope and nationality-specific May endpoint; avoided equating decision receipt with implementation.

summary: Lithuania restricted entry by nonexempt foreigners and ordinary departures by its citizens from 16 March 2020 as part of its COVID-19 quarantine measures. Residents, transport crews and other authorised groups retained exceptions, and goods movement continued. The citizen-departure prohibition ended on 4 May, while eligible Baltic travellers gained reciprocal access on 15 May. Neither change amounted to unrestricted entry for all nationalities.

verification.notes: Checked separate outbound and Baltic inbound endpoints and substantial exemptions.

summary: Estonia restricted entry by nonexempt foreigners from 17 March 2020 to limit COVID-19, while allowing citizens, residents, essential personnel and authorised return transit. Departure was not prohibited. Eligible Baltic travellers could cross the Latvian border again from 15 May, when barriers were removed and cars resumed passage at Ikla. This reopening did not extend equally to all foreign visitors or establish reopening of the Russian frontier.

verification.notes: Checked actual Ikla opening within Baltic eligibility rules and preserved outbound freedom.

summary: Latvia restricted nonexempt passenger movement at its Russian and Belarusian land borders from 17 March 2020 under COVID-19 emergency rules. Freight continued, citizens and residents could return, and authorised departures and humanitarian journeys had separate exceptions. The original legal order ended in June, but replacement restrictions continued and later eased for eligible travellers. The legal change did not itself reopen these borders to every passenger in both directions.

verification.notes: Checked asymmetric exceptions and June legal succession; omitted unresolved shared endpoint and retained successor distinction.

summary: Croatia restricted nonessential personal border crossing from 19 March 2020 during the COVID-19 emergency. Citizens returning home and specified residence, work, medical, freight and transit journeys remained permitted, with further exceptions introduced later. On 28 May, Croatia exempted nationals of ten named EU countries from this prohibition. That was a selective change in travel eligibility, rather than proof that all border traffic had previously stopped or that every foreign visitor could now enter.

verification.notes: Checked bidirectional legal order and selective ten-nationality endpoint.

summary: Slovak hauliers restricted commercial trucks at Vyšné Nemecké–Uzhhorod from 1 to 4 December 2023, demanding restored permit requirements for Ukrainian carriers. Ordinary trucks were admitted at a reduced rate, while humanitarian and military consignments, fuel, animals and fresh or refrigerated goods had exceptions. Passenger cars and buses continued. Normal freight processing resumed on 4 December; remaining queues were not evidence that the blockade continued.

verification.notes: Checked deliberate throughput restriction, exemptions and actual December 4 clearance; separate from later recurrence.

summary: Kosovo restricted land entry by foreign travellers from 14 March 2020 as part of its COVID-19 response. Citizens could return, initially subject to isolation. The government authorised six posts to reopen on 1 June, with actual traffic reported at Vërmicë, while testing and isolation conditions varied by traveller group and changed during the reopening. This did not establish simultaneous unrestricted access at every post or for every nationality.

verification.notes: Checked citizen exemption, six-post permission and Vërmicë operation without extending freight or health conditions universally.

summary: Greece restricted passenger entry from Albania and North Macedonia on 15 March 2020 to limit COVID-19 transmission. Greek citizens, qualifying residents and specified other groups retained exceptions, while freight trucks continued. Evzoni, on the North Macedonian frontier, reopened to ordinary eligible passenger travel in May 2021. That crossing-specific change does not establish the same reopening date for other posts or the Albanian frontier.

verification.notes: Checked Evzoni-only endpoint and admission exceptions rather than complete bilateral closure.

summary: Bulgaria introduced restrictions on arrivals from specified COVID-19 risk areas in March 2020 and then barred many nonexempt third-country entrants from 20 March. Citizens, qualifying residents, family members and authorised transport and essential personnel retained exceptions. Permissions broadened during May and June for selected nationalities and origins. The initial order’s April deadline was not an observed general reopening, and later rules continued to distinguish between traveller categories.

verification.notes: Checked initial ordered window, staged origin/nationality scope and later easing without invented April reopening.

summary: Romania prohibited entry by most nonexempt third-country nationals and stateless people from 22 March 2020 under COVID-19 measures. Romanian, EU, EEA and Swiss citizens were outside that defined category, while specified family, residence, work, humanitarian and transit journeys remained permitted. The prohibition was repealed from 1 June 2021 after changes to its exceptions. It restricted admission eligibility rather than stopping all operations at Romania’s checkpoints.

verification.notes: Checked foreigner category, March effective time and June repeal rather than announcement/publication dates.

summary: Slovak hauliers renewed their protest at Vyšné Nemecké on 11 December 2023, blocking trucks entering Slovakia from Ukraine over opposition to permit-free Ukrainian haulage access. Passenger travel and trucks travelling toward Ukraine were unaffected. Limited inbound truck processing resumed on 13 December, followed by removal of the blockade on 14 December. The partial resumption therefore preceded the return to normal access.

verification.notes: Checked inbound-only freight scope and distinct partial/full December endpoints.

summary: Greece closed the Kastanies–Pazarkule gate on 28 February 2020 during a confrontation over migrant entry from Turkey. The gate remained unavailable for ordinary passenger passage as pandemic restrictions subsequently shaped access; an announced July 2020 reopening did not take place. Restricted passenger operations resumed on 3 July 2021, with Greek and EU citizens admitted while Turkish nationals still faced limited exceptions. Other Greece–Turkey crossings followed separate arrangements.

verification.notes: Preferred contemporary February onset; checked failed 2020 plan and actual restricted July 2021 passage.

summary: Finland restricted nonessential passenger entry and use of secondary land routes from 19 March 2020 to limit COVID-19. Returning citizens, goods and necessary travel retained exceptions, with work permissions changing over time. Ordinary entry across the Norwegian land frontier was restored on 15 June. Sweden and Russia followed different arrangements, and advice against overseas travel did not remove Finnish citizens’ constitutional right to leave.

verification.notes: Checked Norway-only endpoint, route versus traveller restrictions and distinct exit rights.

summary: San Marino ordered secondary roads at its Italian border closed from 5 May 2020 under COVID-19 measures, while keeping six main routes available. Police could authorise additional temporary or timed openings for permitted traffic. The government ordered the blocked routes reopened on 19 May, ahead of the original end-of-May deadline. San Marino was therefore not completely isolated, and the order does not establish the exact reopening time of every road.

verification.notes: Checked six-route exceptions, police discretion and legal early reopening without invented road observations.

summary: Latvia prohibited nonessential entry by many passengers arriving from European countries from 11 February 2021 as part of its COVID-19 response. The measure affected international passenger carriers, including buses and trains, but exempted specified European nationals and residence holders travelling in noncommercial vehicles, alongside essential travel and transport staff. Selected entry restrictions were lifted on 16 June. Testing, vaccination and isolation rules continued to differ between traveller groups.

verification.notes: Checked major private-vehicle nationality exemption; avoided generic Europe-wide traveller shutdown.

summary: Slovenia prohibited nonexempt citizens and residents from travelling to countries on its COVID-19 red list from 29 March 2021. Vaccinated or recovered people and specified work, education, transport, landholding and urgent journeys had exceptions. The Constitutional Court suspended the departure prohibition on 8 April. That decision concerned travel out of Slovenia and did not itself remove quarantine requirements for people entering the country.

verification.notes: Checked outbound rule’s own onset and court stay, distinct from lockdown and inbound health rules.

summary: England expressly prohibited overseas departure without a reasonable excuse from 29 March 2021 during the COVID-19 emergency, including journeys through the Channel Tunnel. Work and other listed needs qualified, and specified transport workers, hauliers and diplomats were exempt. The prohibition was removed on 17 May. This was an England-specific travel rule, not a closure of Northern Ireland’s land border or proof that all international train traffic had stopped.

verification.notes: Checked England-only jurisdiction, Channel Tunnel applicability, exceptions and May statutory removal.

summary: Farmers obstructed roads along the Spain–France and Spain–Andorra frontiers in June 2024, demanding import controls, priority for local production and tax relief. At Biriatou, freight towards France was blocked from the morning of 3 June until the following morning. Other approaches had different openings and exceptions, including overnight breaks. Heavy-vehicle traffic resumed before the remaining queues cleared, so congestion afterward is not counted as continuing closure.

verification.notes: Checked Biriatou reported 24-hour period and differentiated other sites, directions and queue clearance.

summary: Greek farmers briefly blocked cars and lorries at the Kulata–Promachonas crossing with Bulgaria on 31 January 2017. They were protesting tax and social-security changes and seeking greater subsidies. Traffic resumed in both directions after roughly an hour, while other frontier crossings remained available. Reports give approximate times, so the incident is recorded as a short same-day interruption rather than a full-day closure.

verification.notes: Checked vehicle scope, protest demands, approximate one-hour clearance and alternative posts.

summary: Sweden required most nonexempt foreign arrivals from Denmark, including travellers over the Öresund link, to present a negative COVID-19 test taken within 48 hours from 28 December 2021. Citizens, residents, freight personnel and other eligible groups had exceptions. From 21 January 2022, vaccination or recovery evidence and a longer testing window became acceptable for the relevant arrivals. The change eased conditional admission rather than reopening a completely closed bridge.

verification.notes: Checked negative-test-only phase and successor certificates; did not invent original complete exemption roster.

summary: The Orlivka–Isaccea ferry crossing between Ukraine and Romania suspended passage on 26 September 2023 after overnight Russian attacks raised safety concerns. People and vehicles using that route were affected, although vehicles already inside the Romanian checkpoint could complete inward processing. Border passage resumed that evening. The interruption concerned this ferry crossing and was separate from another attack-related suspension in October.

verification.notes: Checked same-day actual restart, already-entered vehicle exception and separation from October episode.

summary: The Orlivka–Isaccea ferry crossing between Ukraine and Romania suspended admission of people and vehicles on 6 October 2023 following an attack and related safety concerns. Border controls resumed in both directions for all vehicle categories on 15 October, with contemporary reporting confirming ferry operations. Accounts differ about the subsequent service timetable, but that disagreement does not alter the documented return of admission at the crossing.

verification.notes: Checked actual October 15 restoration and distinguished timetable conflict from reopening date.

summary: Finland and Norway require herders to keep reindeer from crossing their shared divide for ordinary grazing, using fencing and guarding duties set out in bilateral agreements. A renewed convention took effect on 1 January 2017, continuing an older restriction. It allows designated transit routes without grazing, return of stray animals and properly controlled slaughter imports. The measure regulates reindeer husbandry; it does not prevent people generally from crossing the border.

verification.notes: Checked renewed rather than original onset, operative grazing divide and treaty transit/stray/slaughter exceptions.

summary: Farmers blocked frontier road traffic near Siret on the Romania–Ukraine border for about three hours on 7 April 2023. They complained that competition from Ukrainian grain was harming their livelihoods. The available account does not distinguish every vehicle category or direction affected. Later truck processing and congestion, including disruption associated with earlier snow restrictions, do not establish that the protest blockade continued beyond that afternoon.

verification.notes: Checked short protest episode and attributed grain grievance; kept unresolved traffic scope and weather/queue distinction.

summary: Truck passage at Siret–Porubne on the Romania–Ukraine border was blocked on 13 January 2024, while cars, buses and pedestrians continued to be processed normally. Freight processing resumed later the same day. The immediate motive for this specific action was not established in the initial account; reports about the preceding day’s regional protests cannot by themselves supply it. Later blockades at Siret are recorded separately.

verification.notes: Checked truck-only same-day interruption and uncertainty of this specific episode’s motive.

summary: Protesters again obstructed the Romanian approach road to Siret–Porubne on 14 January 2024, affecting freight access near the Ukrainian border. Romanian police reported obstruction in both directions and normal traffic restored that evening; an earlier Ukrainian notice had still described outward processing as normal. Reported demands concerned fuel taxes, insurance and regulatory changes. The differing observations do not establish identical restrictions on every vehicle or direction throughout the day.

verification.notes: Checked local road obstruction versus checkpoint processing, attributed demands and same-day restoration.

summary: Protesters blocked freight trucks in both directions at Siret–Porubne from 15 January 2024, citing grain prices and livelihood concerns. Small cars could continue through an unobstructed lane. Trucks leaving Romania began moving again by 17 January, while trucks entering from Ukraine remained blocked. The initial two-way freight blockade therefore ended with a partial reopening, followed by a separate period of restriction in the remaining direction.

verification.notes: Checked truck-only scope, actual outward partial resumption and relation to remaining-direction phase.

summary: Trucks entering Romania from Ukraine remained blocked at Siret–Porubne after outward freight traffic partly resumed on 17 January 2024. Protesters continued the same campaign over grain competition and livelihoods, while cars passed and trucks leaving Romania were admitted in limited groups. Normal traffic in both directions returned overnight on 19–20 January. This was the remaining part of the blockade begun on 15 January, not a new independent protest.

verification.notes: Checked directional continuation, limited outward flow and overnight final endpoint.

summary: Protesters restricted eligible truck traffic at Vicovu de Sus–Krasnoilsk on the Romania–Ukraine border in January 2024 during the wider agricultural and transport protests. The action paused overnight on 15 January and resumed the next morning, so it was not an uninterrupted four-day closure. Empty lorries were reported moving again on 19 January. Cars and pedestrians remained permitted, and the crossing’s truck eligibility should not be extended to all heavy freight.

verification.notes: Checked overnight gap, eligible empty-lorry scope and January 19 resumption.

summary: Machinery used by protesters blocked the Romanian approach to Halmeu–Dyakove in January 2024, amid demands opposing Ukrainian grain imports. Ukrainian customs suspended trucks travelling into Romania on 18 January to prevent freight queues obstructing passenger access; cars and buses continued. Romanian officials began accepting cargo vehicles again on 20 January. The documented suspension concerns that freight direction and does not establish an identical two-way closure.

verification.notes: Checked approach blockade and protective Ukrainian suspension, passenger exceptions and actual directional resumption.

summary: The Orlivka–Isaccea ferry crossing between Ukraine and Romania suspended people, vehicles and goods after an overnight attack on 1 September 2026. Ferry operations resumed in stages on 2 September, although another official account dates customs restoration to the following morning. A further attack caused a separate interruption overnight on 5–6 September, with processing restored that morning. The reopening between the attacks prevents treating them as one continuous closure.

verification.notes: Checked differing operational/customs endpoints and separate September recurrence; no targeting intent inferred.

summary: Yellow-vest protesters obstructed several French border approaches on 22 December 2018, including Le Boulou towards Spain, Ventimiglia towards Italy and Strasbourg’s Pont de l’Europe. Traffic restrictions differed by site: some actions targeted freight while cars continued, and the Strasbourg obstruction was brief. The demonstrations ended that day at different times. Clearance of protesters and road cleaning did not always establish when normal vehicle passage resumed.

verification.notes: Checked multi-site same-day scope and Ventimiglia motorway identification; no shared duration or invented first passage.

summary: Portuguese farmers blocked roads to Spain at Paymogo–Minas de Santo Domingo and Rosal de la Frontera–Vila Verde de Ficalho from 1 February 2024 over agricultural-policy grievances. Ordinary vehicles were obstructed in both directions, with emergency passage allowed and other crossings available. Both blockades continued into the following day. Ficalho returned to normal overnight on 2–3 February; the same reopening date is not established for Paymogo.

verification.notes: Checked two-site continued obstruction and Ficalho-only endpoint, emergency exception and restrained motive attribution.

summary: Albanian authorities stopped vehicles entering from Kosovo at Morinë on 31 March 2018 after a protest against Kalimash road tolls blocked the onward route. Some Albanian-plated cars were allowed through during the interruption, and the crossing reopened later that afternoon. Reports describe a restriction lasting only a few hours. It affected entry into Albania, rather than all movement through the Kosovo–Albania frontier.

verification.notes: Checked onward-road trigger, inbound direction, partial plate exception and same-day reopening.

summary: Croatian authorities closed the Maljevac–Velika Kladuša crossing with Bosnia and Herzegovina on 24 October 2018 during a confrontation involving migrants, citing safety concerns. Passenger and freight traffic stopped in both directions at the named post, with alternative crossings available. The crossing reopened on 30 October, and vehicles were reported using it again. The closure did not cover the entire Croatian–Bosnian border.

verification.notes: Checked all-traffic named-post scope and actual October 30 restoration.

summary: War veterans blocked road access at Bijača on the Bosnia and Herzegovina–Croatia border on 2 July 2018, seeking service-related payments and changes to the veterans’ registry. The blockade began around noon and the crossing resumed operation before the evening after police intervened. Reports do not separately establish every vehicle category or direction affected. Earlier protest actions are distinct from this short episode.

verification.notes: Checked veterans’ demands, same-day police clearance and unresolved detailed traffic scope.

summary: Montenegrin transporters blocked commercial freight at participating land-border terminals from 26 to 29 January 2026 during a regional drivers’ protest. The action concerned drivers’ travel and employment conditions and domestic transport demands; passenger travel and specified cargo, including medicines and live animals, were exempt. The blockades were withdrawn after negotiations. The evidence records a multi-day campaign, while exact operating times and exceptions differed between terminals.

verification.notes: Checked realised 72-hour campaign, nine land-post roster, passenger/Port Bar exclusion and January withdrawal.

summary: Transporters in Bosnia and Herzegovina blocked commercial freight entering and leaving participating border terminals from 26 January 2026, protesting Schengen limits on drivers’ stays. Passenger traffic continued, with additional emergency and cargo exceptions reported at Bijača. Drivers began withdrawing on 30 January and clearance was still underway that afternoon. Reports directly identify Gradiška and Bijača but do not establish identical starting and ending times at every terminal.

verification.notes: Checked country campaign, direct gate evidence, local exemptions and withdrawal versus completed clearance.

summary: Serbian transporters blocked commercial freight at participating border terminals from 26 January 2026 in protest against Schengen stay limits for drivers. Outward obstruction began before inward restrictions, while passengers and specified cargo were exempt. The action was lifted on 30 January as traffic normalised. A later extension to the Montenegro frontier began on 29 January and lasted less than a day, rather than sharing the whole campaign’s timetable.

verification.notes: Checked staggered freight directions, separate shorter Montenegro phase and January 30 lifting.

summary: Transporters blocked freight terminals in North Macedonia from 26 January 2026 during the regional protest against Schengen stay limits for drivers. Commercial cargo movement was affected while passengers were excluded from the action, and reporting directly documented the blockade at Gevgelija–Bogorodica. Freight traffic was restored on 29 January. The association named several participating posts, but its campaign timetable does not establish exact first and last passage at each one.

verification.notes: Checked directly observed Gevgelija action, freight-only scope and time-zone-consistent January restoration.

summary: Montenegrin transporters blocked commercial freight at participating crossings with Serbia and Bosnia and Herzegovina from 14 April 2026, pressing demands over drivers’ stay rules and domestic commitments. Passengers and specified essential cargo generally continued. Police reported traffic restored on 17 April after remaining obstructions were removed. At Dračenovac, protesters briefly extended the action to passenger vehicles for about two hours, a separate escalation from the longer freight-only campaign.

verification.notes: Checked freight campaign and exemptions, April clearance and separate passenger-inclusive extension.

summary: A Greek customs strike interrupted passage at four crossings with Albania on 27 July 2026: Kapshticë, Kakavijë, Qafë Botë and Tre Urat. Customs staff were protesting unpaid overtime and shift compensation and inadequate funding allocations. Vehicles and travellers were delayed for several hours before processing resumed that day. Reported starting times differ, particularly at Kapshticë, so the scheduled strike window is not treated as an exact duration at every post.

verification.notes: Checked original union grievances, four posts and same-day actual interruptions rather than single scheduled duration.

summary: Turkish Cypriot authorities had suspended ordinary passage at Lefka–Apliki, Deryneia and the Limnitis route by the beginning of 2021 under COVID-19 restrictions. These crossings reopened conditionally on 4 June, with testing rules applying to eligible passengers, including third-country nationals; passage was recorded in both directions. The first suspension date is not established, and the earlier Republic of Cyprus closures cannot supply the start of this separate authority-side restriction.

verification.notes: Checked beginning-year snapshot, actual June passage and distinction from Republic-side earlier suspensions.

summary: Latvia prohibited entry on foot or by bicycle at Pāternieki, Terehova and Grebņeva from 19 March 2025, citing security and migration concerns. Pāternieki faces Belarus, while the other two posts face Russia. Eligible travellers could still enter in motor vehicles under the applicable rules. The order specifically concerned entry into Latvia; it does not by itself establish the same prohibition on departure or a closure of the posts to all traffic.

verification.notes: Checked entry-specific wording, frontier pairs, motor-vehicle exception and absence of verified later endpoint.

summary: Protesters blocked the road to Urziceni–Vállaj on the Romania–Hungary border in both directions on 17 January 2024. Reporting associated the protest with farmers’ concerns about grain prices and Ukrainian imports, although the affected crossing was with Hungary. The obstruction was removed after discussions with the prefect, and traffic resumed after roughly two hours. It was a separate short action from blockades at Romania’s Ukrainian crossings.

verification.notes: Checked Hungary geography, attributed grain grievance and brief same-day clearance.

summary: Yellow-vest protesters obstructed heavy trucks at the Biriatou toll-road approach to the France–Spain border early on 22 December 2018. Gendarmes cleared the obstruction after roughly three hours that morning. The reports identify freight vehicles but do not establish the direction affected or the specific demands of this group. Other yellow-vest actions at different crossings that day followed separate timetables.

verification.notes: Checked heavy-truck scope, approximate three-hour action and no invented local motive or direction.

summary: Ukraine restricted outward travel by most male citizens aged 18–60 from 24 February 2022 under martial law following Russia’s invasion. Defined exemptions allowed some men to leave. From 28 August 2025, most men aged 18–22 could travel abroad with the required documents, while specified officeholders remained restricted. The general restriction continued for nonexempt men aged 23–60, with further profession-specific permissions; it did not prohibit departure by every Ukrainian citizen.

verification.notes: Checked age-cohort change and exceptions; did not treat August easing as universal exit reopening.

summary: Moldovan farmers repeatedly blocked vehicle access to Leușeni–Albița on the Romanian border during February 2024, demanding promised diesel support and compensation for maize and sunflower crops. Separate actions occurred on several days, with traffic restored between them. The first reopening time is uncertain, and an ambulance was reported obstructed during one later action. These were recurring road blockades, rather than one continuous closure across the whole protest period.

verification.notes: Checked seven separate dates and reopened gaps, specific demands and documented ambulance obstruction.

summary: A Greek customs strike stopped cars and buses at Kakavijë and Kapshticë on the Albanian border on 30 May 2018. Limited passage on foot and medical emergencies were reported as exceptions. Notices announced a 24-hour stoppage, but the recorded evidence does not confirm when normal vehicle processing actually resumed. The underlying workers’ demands are not established, and differing reported times prevent a precise shared duration for both crossings.

verification.notes: Checked actual vehicle interruption, exceptions and scheduled rather than observed next-day ending.

summary: Hungarian authorities interrupted road traffic at Tompa–Kelebia on the Serbian border on 6 February 2020, citing safety concerns and the inability to ensure unobstructed passage. The crossing reopened early the following morning. A separate interruption on 8 February affected only the inbound freight gate for less than an hour; passengers in both directions and outbound freight were unaffected. The two episodes therefore had different traffic scopes.

verification.notes: Checked police timing, safety attribution and separate inbound-freight-only recurrence.

summary: Estonia closed the Narva 2–Parusinka pedestrian crossing with Russia on 28 November 2022, directing eligible users to the main Narva 1 crossing. The initiating explanation concerned renovation and concentration of staff and resources, rather than a security closure of the whole frontier. A later ministerial account declined to reopen the same pedestrian post because of staffing constraints. The main road crossing followed its own separate restrictions.

verification.notes: Checked actual local pedestrian closure, alternative post and administrative rather than invented security rationale.

summary: Road vehicles were barred from the Narva 1–Ivangorod crossing between Estonia and Russia from 1 February 2024 during reconstruction, while pedestrians retained access. Estonia later restricted pedestrian opening hours, first to 07:00–23:00 from May 2024 and then to 07:00–19:00 from June 2026. These were separate vehicle and overnight pedestrian restrictions. The projected completion date for reconstruction did not establish that road traffic had resumed.

verification.notes: Checked three distinct traffic/hour phases and rejected construction target as reopening.

summary: Lithuania diverted incoming freight trains from Belarus away from Stasylos–Benekainys to Kena from 16 February 2023, citing anti-smuggling requirements. The measure concerned international arrivals, while the domestic Stasylos station continued operating. Later rules described broader cross-border restrictions, but these are not assumed to have applied from the original date. Planned inspection equipment and future timetable arrangements do not establish an actual reopening of the international route.

verification.notes: Checked initial inbound scope, anti-smuggling reason, continued domestic station and unverified operational endpoint.

summary: Estonia introduced recurring overnight closures at the Koidula and Luhamaa road crossings with Russia from 24 February 2026. Pedestrians and vehicles could still cross during the daytime. Officials linked the reduced hours to staffing, security and customs-enforcement needs, and later decisions continued the arrangement. The measure was a restriction on operating hours at two posts, rather than a continuous closure of the entire frontier.

verification.notes: Checked recurring night regime, both traveller modes, daytime access and later continuation.

summary: Norway restricted entry by nonexempt Russian-registered passenger cars from 3 October 2023 under its sanctions regime. The measure included temporary imports of vehicles with nine or fewer seats, while larger vehicles and specified citizenship, residence, diplomatic and humanitarian cases had exceptions. It applied to the vehicle’s admission, including at Storskog, rather than automatically prohibiting every occupant from entering Norway. No final lifting date is established in the recorded evidence.

verification.notes: Checked vehicle class and conditional exceptions; distinguished vehicle sanction from passenger admission and no invented repeal.

summary: Finland began restricting entry by nonexempt Russian-registered passenger vehicles on 16 September 2023 under EU sanctions. The affected category included cars, camper vans and small minibuses, with specified citizenship, residence, family, diplomatic and humanitarian exceptions. Later guidance on vehicles already admitted did not reopen the border to new imports generally. Travellers’ personal eligibility to enter Finland remained a separate question from whether their vehicle could be brought in.

verification.notes: Checked customs commodity scope, exceptions and previously admitted vehicles versus new entry.

summary: Estonia restricted Russian-registered vehicle entry through its external border from 13 September 2023, implementing sanctions on vehicle imports. Departure and movement within the EU remained possible, and a traveller otherwise entitled to enter could cross without the vehicle. Later guidance continued the rule while identifying specified exceptions. This was a restriction on vehicle admission, rather than a prohibition on every Russian national or all movement at the crossings.

verification.notes: Checked external inbound scope, sanctions attribution, person/vehicle distinction and later qualified exceptions.

summary: Norway prohibited nonexempt Russian-established road-haulage companies from carrying goods into the country from 29 April 2022 under sanctions, with implementation documented at Storskog. Limited grace arrangements applied to specified journeys already underway, and postal or authorised goods movements had exceptions. Cargo carried by a different eligible operator could still move. That distinction means continued freight traffic did not by itself show that restrictions on Russian carriers had ended.

verification.notes: Checked carrier rather than all-cargo scope, grace/exemptions and operator substitution distinction.

summary: Lithuania restricted rail transit of selected sanctioned goods between mainland Russia and Kaliningrad in June 2022, initially including steel and ferrous metals. Passenger trains and nonsanctioned cargo continued. Revised arrangements in July allowed conditional essential-goods transit, with later evidence of cement passing through Kena. That did not establish an unrestricted reopening for every commodity: quotas and separate restrictions on military, dual-use, luxury and road transport remained.

verification.notes: Checked commodity-specific onset, July legal versus actual cement return and continuing separate limits.

summary: Bulgarian grain growers repeatedly blocked road approaches to Romania in March and April 2023, protesting agricultural imports and their reported effects on prices and livelihoods. Actions affected Ruse–Giurgiu, Kardam–Negru Vodă, Vidin–Calafat and a diversion route at Durankulak, with traffic and directions varying by site. Most documented blocks lasted hours, with movement restored between actions. The separate demonstrations do not constitute one continuous closure across all these crossings.

verification.notes: Checked nine distinct phases/observations, varying sites and directions, attributed demands and reopened gaps.

summary: Bulgarian farmers disrupted road access at Ruse–Giurgiu and Kardam–Negru Vodă on 18 September 2023. At Ruse, cars and trucks were blocked in both directions during a short action linked to compensation grievances. At Kardam, a protest over grain imports restricted vehicle entry into Bulgaria, with traffic restored earlier than the announced finish. The two posts had different traffic rules and timings, rather than forming one general frontier closure.

verification.notes: Checked separate local motives, Ruse two-way versus Kardam inbound scope and actual early reopening.

summary: Bulgarian farmers blocked approaches to several Romanian crossings on 6–7 February 2024, pressing demands over support, production costs and agricultural policy. Actions at Ruse, Vidin, Durankulak and Kardam differed in length and traffic scope. At Vidin, trucks were affected in both directions while some outbound cars could use a detour. Traffic resumed between daily actions, so consecutive protest dates do not establish an uninterrupted overnight closure.

verification.notes: Checked six daily/site episodes, Vidin directional detour and preserved gaps.

summary: Greek farmers blocked passenger and freight vehicles at Evzoni–Bogorodica on the North Macedonian frontier from 30 January to 17 February 2017. Protesters sought changes to taxes and social contributions and talks with the government. Pedestrian passage and some perishable-goods trucks were reported as exceptions, while other crossings offered alternatives at particular times. Tractors were removed and vehicle passage resumed on 17 February; the availability of exceptions throughout the blockade is uncertain.

verification.notes: Checked local protest rationale, repeated closure evidence, actual clearance and limited exception evidence.

summary: Greek farmers intermittently blocked the Kalpaki road approach serving Kakavia and Mertzani in February 2024. Ordinary road traffic was affected, but buses and vulnerable travellers were allowed through, and reports explicitly describe an intervening opening. Later sit-ins and symbolic actions continued over several days. The evidence concerns an approach road, not closure of the customs posts themselves, and does not establish a final local ending date or continuous daily obstruction.

verification.notes: Checked intermittent road-only action, openings and exceptions; did not import generic national demands.

summary: Latvia restricted entry by Russian-registered vehicles at its Russian and Belarusian borders from 12 September 2023 under EU sanctions. Specified diplomatic and consular vehicles were exempt, and qualifying vehicles could still leave the EU through Latvia. Later guidance continued to distinguish the border-entry rule from separate restrictions on using vehicles already inside the country. The measure concerned vehicles, rather than automatically denying entry to every Russian traveller.

verification.notes: Checked September 12 effective rule, geographic scope, contemporary diplomatic exception and separate domestic use.

summary: Lithuania began restricting entry by Russian-registered passenger cars on 11 September 2023, with customs turnbacks reported during the following week. A qualified exception allowed Russian citizens to transit to or from Kaliningrad using a simplified transit document, with the vehicle owner present and the journey completed within 24 hours. These conditions were documented by late September. They permitted specified transit rather than general entry by Russian-registered cars.

verification.notes: Checked actual early enforcement and late-September documented transit conditions without backdating every clause.

summary: Poland restricted entry by Russian-registered passenger cars from 17 September 2023 as part of sanctions implementation. The announced rule applied to the car regardless of the driver’s citizenship, and an early refusal was reported the following day. Later customs evidence records another attempted inward car import stopped at Terespol in August 2026. These observations support continued enforcement of the rule without establishing every exemption or daily crossing decision.

verification.notes: Checked announcement/effective dates, September 18 refusal and later scoped enforcement; no complete exemption claim.
